notes: Scope: the six ACME investigations in PSI (PSI-20 BRE, PSI-21 CLD Flame, PSI-22 E-FIELD Flames, PSI-10 Flame Design, PSI-23 s-Flame, PSI-159 CFI-G). All flight data are microgravity; none of these sources holds partial-gravity data. Lunar base, Mars base and pressurized rover appear in environment_relevance only where the atmosphere (elevated oxygen, reduced pressure) matches, so those uses are extrapolations in gravity.

Quotes keep the characters of the saved source text with runs of whitespace collapsed to one space. PDF line-break hyphens therefore show as "steady- state" or "second- round", the ACME fact sheet keeps its ligature characters, and PSI table quotes are raw CSV rows. In the BRE final report pdftotext renders the Greek delta of the heat of combustion symbol as the private-use character U+F044; it is kept in three quotes and can be shown as a delta.

Main gap filled: the NTRS abstracts for ACME are thin, so the final reports that PSI stores with each investigation were downloaded (one request at a time) and saved under raw/pdf as PSI-<n>_<slug>.pdf with pdftotext output: BRE, E-FIELD Flames, s-Flame, Flame Design and CFI-G final reports, plus the 2022 Central States Section paper filed under PSI-20 Presentations. NTRS PDFs saved as raw/pdf/<id>.pdf: 20210021781, 20210022542, 20140009169, 20170009141, 20160010073, 20150011070, 20150002322, 20040053549, 20010074022, 20050195844, 20010074032, 20250001364. Fetch log: raw/pdf/_acme_fetchlog.jsonl. No request failed.

CLD Flame: PSI-21 holds only metadata, the experimental table and raw data (no report or science document), and NTRS has no paper with its ISS results. Its 5 findings come from the NASA ACME fact sheet and the 2021 NASA paper (NTRS 20210021781), and are less quantitative than the other five investigations (the SLICE abstract finding ACME-032 was rejected by the verifier as a SLICE result). The fact sheet gives two soot figures (five to eight times in Selected Findings, nearly a factor of ten in the overview); the measured five-to-eight figure is the one recorded.

Sources that gave nothing usable: NTRS posters 20210015913 and 20220015583 are image-only PDFs (empty pdftotext output); NTRS records 27482090396921, 17720132749449, 28516810543238, 31112159710975, 25983543780692, 10022129583755 and 30580252934587 (journal papers on BRE, CFI-G, Flame Design and E-FIELD Flames) carry a title and DOI but no abstract and no download, so nothing is quoted from them (their JSON is saved under raw/pdf for the record). NTRS 20040053549 and 20010074022 (radiant extinction of spherical flames) belong to a different investigator team and are not attributed to s-Flame.

BRE oxygen limit: the sources state it three ways and each is kept as its own finding: self-extinction below about 25% oxygen (2021 NASA paper), quasi-steady flames at oxygen mole fractions of 0.265 and above with all normal-atmosphere flames out within 40 s (2022 final report), and self-extinction at 21% versus continued burning at elevated oxygen (PSI record). The final report calls its results preliminary.

Final reports label their results preliminary and several statements are hedged in the source ("seem to", "appear to"); claims keep that hedging. decision_hint and earth_instinct are interpretation written for VESTA, not NASA text.

PSI table quality: the BRE table has two cells reading "3400%" and "2100%" (meant as 34 and 21), the CLD Flame table has drag-fill damage in "Fuel Bottle" (40% CH5 ... CH14) and the s-Flame table in "Atmosphere*" (N3 ... N6). Those cells are not quoted. Oxygen and pressure ranges in the investigation records that come from PSI tables are supported by quoted rows.
psi_url is the PSI page pattern https://psi.nasa.gov/physci/repo/data/investigations/<accession> described in psi-access.md; its source entry quotes the accession from the raw PSI record.

Source years: the ACME fact sheet PDF sits under nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/07 and is given year 2025, although most of its text was written before flight (it says testing is expected to begin in 2017). The E-FIELD Flames final report is titled "(2019)" and dated 10 April 2021. PSI record years are the PSI release year.

Not in these sources for ACME: flame spread rates over solids, smoke particle sizes, detector response and tests of suppression agents. BRE did not run its desired O2/CO2 atmospheres; s-Flame used helium and nitrogen as diluents of the fuel and atmosphere, not as an applied suppressant.

Verifier pass (2026-11-14): 75 findings checked against the sentences around each quote; 74 kept (23 with fields narrowed, quotes untouched), 1 rejected (ACME-032). Details in evidence/acme.rejects.md. Each kept finding carries a "verified" note.

Live re-download check: the NTRS 20210021781 full-text PDF and the nasa.gov ACME fact sheet PDF were downloaded again and are byte-identical (sha256) to the cached PDFs, and pdftotext -layout of each reproduces the cached text; the nasa.gov article "Cool Flames Created During a First for International Space Station Research" was downloaded again and contains the three quoted passages; the NTRS abstract 20150002322 was confirmed live by quotecheck --refetch. psi.nasa.gov could not be re-checked: the PSI web service answered HTTP 500 (PSI-20 record, 5 tries) and 504 (PSI-20 and PSI-23 final reports and the CFI-G normal-flame table, 3 tries each), so the PSI-hosted files were checked only against their cached copies (each of the five cached final-report .txt files equals pdftotext -layout of the cached PDF, and file ids and byte sizes match raw/psi/files/PSI-<n>.json).

investigations.name: BRE
investigations.full_name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments - Burning Rate Emulator
investigations.hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) with the ACME chamber insert and flat porous BRE burners of 25 and 50 mm diameter
investigations.years: 2019-2021 (ISS tests February to April 2019 and September 2020 to January 2021)
investigations.objectives: Establish the burning conditions in a quiescent microgravity ambient in terms of material properties: observe burning behavior, including extinction limits, of methane/nitrogen and ethylene/nitrogen mixtures on porous circular burners in O2/N2 ambients of various pressures and oxygen concentrations, including atmospheres NASA considers for human missions.
investigations.sample_geometry: Flat porous circular gas burners of 25 mm and 50 mm diameter that emulate a flat condensed-fuel surface; a dome-shaped flame forms over the burner.

conditions.pressure: 14.7 psia, 10.2 psia and 8.2 psia atmospheres examined; more tests at roughly atmospheric pressure
conditions.flow: quiescent chamber, no forced air flow; fuel fed through the burner (example: 2.3 g/m2s in test 19070K1)

investigations.variables: Varied: fuel (ethylene, nitrogen-diluted ethylene, methane), burner diameter (25 or 50 mm), fuel flow rate, ambient oxygen concentration and chamber pressure. Held: O2/N2 atmosphere with no air flow. Round one used ethylene and the 25 mm burner; round two added methane and the 50 mm burner. Desired O2/CO2 atmospheres were not tested.
measurements: heat flux to the burner (two heat flux transducers per burner)
flame temperature by thin filament pyrometry

investigations.name: Flame Design
investigations.full_name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Flame Design
investigations.hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) with the ACME chamber insert and a porous stainless-steel spherical burner
investigations.years: 2019-2022 (ISS tests April to July 2019 and October 2021 to February 2022)
investigations.pi: Richard L. Axelbaum (Washington University in St. Louis)
investigations.objectives: Obtain soot-inception limits and extinction limits of quasi-steady normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames as functions of flow rate, stoichiometric mixture fraction, amount of inert and pressure, with detailed measurements, and evaluate whether steady flames can exist.
fuels: ethylene (C2H4), pure and diluted with nitrogen
investigations.sample_geometry: Porous stainless-steel spherical burner in the chamber: normal flames (fuel flows from the burner into an oxygen/nitrogen atmosphere) and inverse flames (oxygen/nitrogen flows from the burner into a nitrogen/ethylene atmosphere).

conditions.o2_percent: normal flames: ambient oxygen mole fraction 0.2 to 0.38 (limit 40%); inverse flames: burner supply oxygen mole fraction 0.4 to 0.85
conditions.pressure: published extinction results at 1 bar; chamber pressure was also varied (the PSI inverse-flame table lists an initial pressure of 3.0 atm in some tests)
conditions.flow: quiescent chamber; constant reactant flow from the burner, total mass flow 0.6 to 12.2 mg/s (normal) and 2.3 to 11.3 mg/s (inverse)

investigations.variables: Varied: reactant flow rate, fuel dilution and oxygen concentration (stoichiometric mixture fraction, adiabatic flame temperature), chamber pressure, and flow direction (normal or inverse flame). Held: ethylene with nitrogen as inert (one propane day), spherical burner. Methane, CO2 diluent and coflow flames were not tested.
measurements: broad and narrow-band flame emission (photomultiplier tubes)
